summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired confirmatory study with complete archived artifacts. The experiment and analysis are reproducible and conservative. The principal scientific finding is null/near-ceiling: ungated gpt-5-mini generation already produced 199/200 emulator-executable configurations and the bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline produced 200/200 (paired difference 0.005, 95% CI [0.0,0.015], exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0). The manuscript is generally sound and properly cautious, but it requires a small set of clarifications to avoid potential misinterpretation (not new experiments).
critical_issues: Insufficient clarity about the shared-initial-generation design choice and its implications for interpretation and generalizability (the guarded and baseline arms used the same initial LLM candidate rather than independently re-sampling).

Ambiguity in the operational definition of “emulator-executable” and the success criterion: the manuscript should explicitly state whether each generated configuration was applied to the emulator, which checks the deterministic validator performed, and precisely what constituted a success vs. a verifier pass.

The manuscript does not explicitly connect the observed near-ceiling baseline to the preregistered target effect. Although CI and null result are reported, the paper should explicitly state that the 95% CI [0.0,0.015] excludes the preregistered 15 percentage-point target and discuss the consequence for the preregistered power assumptions and confirmatory conclusions.
required_revisions: Add a clear Methods paragraph (or expand existing text) that describes the shared_initial_generation protocol: state that a single initial candidate was generated per intent and shared across arms (per preregistration and the execution manifest), explain why this choice was made (model-call budget / design rationale), and explicitly discuss how this choice affects interpretation and external generalizability (i.e., GVR operating on the same candidate versus independent generation per arm). Cite the execution manifest/provider-call audit to support the factual description (no new analysis required).

Explicitly define the success endpoint in Methods and Results: state that success = deterministic_validator_v5 report of 'valid' after applying the generated configuration to the Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator (or, if the validator is a static canonicalizer, state that explicitly). Describe the validator’s checks (syntactic parse, required-command presence, simulated final_state reachability) and cite representative validator_trace artifacts (paths and hashes are already archived).

In Results or Discussion add an explicit sentence quantifying how the observed interval and counts relate to the preregistered target: e.g., note that the 95% bootstrap CI [0.0,0.015] excludes the preregistered 0.15 (15 pp) target and therefore the confirmatory hypothesis of a ≥15 pp improvement is not supported; discuss that the near-ceiling baseline invalidated the original power assumptions and the practical implication (limited ability to detect large absolute improvements). Cite the preregistration power plan and the observed contingency table from the analysis artifacts. No new experiments are required to make this textual clarification.

Add a brief statement in Methods or Discussion explaining the single repair invocation observed (repair stage count=1) and its provenance (which task invoked repair; path to repair trace). Use the archived repair-stage audit in the execution manifest to back this factual statement and discuss how this affected secondary/failure-mode analyses.

Clarify the exact McNemar test variant used and reference the archived analysis artifact (exact_mcnemar_two_sided and bootstrap parameters). Ensure the manuscript reports the contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00) in the Results text (they are present in artifacts) so readers can verify the test inputs.
optional_revisions: Tighten prose in Related Work to focus on the 3–5 most relevant prior systems and explicitly compare experiment scope (task size, emulator fidelity, verifier type).

Include a small table summarizing the distribution of task difficulty levels (easy/medium/hard/very_hard) drawn from the task_manifest to help readers assess external validity (artifact condition_summary/representative_tasks are available).
Add one sentence acknowledging the shared-generation design reduces model-call budget and that independent regeneration could be evaluated in future work (labelled explicitly as future work).
Briefly note in Discussion that adversarial/out-of-distribution intents remain an important open axis and point to the relevant artifacts in the limitations paragraph.
